key_highlights: ASX slumped despite AI rebound on Wall Street, with NAB and BHP among key decliners.
NAB announced significant job cuts of thousands, signalling cost-cutting pressure on major banks.
Critical Resources and Critica table major rare earths and gold plays, boosting small-cap materials interest.
Iron ore weakness is spooking major miners (Vale commentary signals global demand concern), pressuring BHP.AX and RIO.AX.
Oil prices surging ('Oil relentless', 'Oil rockets') — positive for energy sector.
China's export boom flagged as a structural risk; Chinese growth appetite questioned by macro commentators.
Perth house prices entering a bust phase — negative signal for WA-exposed REITs and residential developers.
New home sales dropping fast — headwinds for construction and consumer discretionary sectors.
Manganese jackpot in Pilbara (59.6% grades) and NT rare earths strike extending 8km — junior miners in focus.
AI volatility on Wall Street creating mixed sentiment spillover to ASX tech and growth stocks.

sectors.trend: Mixed. Iron ore weakness pressures large-cap miners. Junior explorers active with rare earths, gold, and manganese discoveries in WA and NT drawing speculative interest.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX and RIO.AX face near-term headwinds from iron ore price softness and China demand uncertainty. Small-cap explorers (rare earths, gold, manganese) offer speculative upside but with elevated risk.

sectors.trend: Bearish. NAB's large-scale job cuts signal margin compression and structural cost pressure across the sector. ASX financials underperformed on the day.
sectors.implications: NAB.AX directly impacted. Sentiment contagion likely to weigh on CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, and WBC.AX. Watch for sector-wide re-rating if job cuts reflect deteriorating loan book quality or revenue outlook.

sectors.trend: Bullish. Oil prices surging with 'Oil relentless' and 'Oil rockets' commentary from macro sources. Energy shares noted as jumping on the ASX.
sectors.implications: Positive for Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX), and Beach Energy (BPT.AX). LNG exporters also benefit from elevated energy prices.

sectors.trend: Volatile. Wall Street AI rebound did not fully translate to ASX. Macro commentary flags 'end of AI 1.0' and louder AI alarm bells, suggesting caution.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names with AI exposure face sentiment headwinds. Investors should be selective; Wall Street AI volatility could spill over further.

sectors.trend: Mildly negative. Banana shortage hitting supermarket shelves due to Queensland weather. New home sales dropping signals broader consumer stress.
sectors.implications: WOW.AX and COL.AX face supply-side cost pressures from produce shortages. Declining home sales weigh on consumer discretionary and construction-linked names.

sectors.trend: Bearish. Perth leading a house price bust. New home sales dropping sharply. Sydney supply overhang ('built it and nobody came').
sectors.implications: Residential-exposed REITs and developers (e.g., Stockland SGP.AX, Mirvac MGR.AX) face downward pressure. Commercial REITs less directly affected but sentiment drag likely.

sectors.trend: Neutral to mildly positive. 'Ozempic face' discovery commentary suggests continued interest in GLP-1 adjacent plays; limited direct ASX headline impact today.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains a defensive anchor. Niche pharma/biotech names with obesity or metabolic drug exposure may see speculative interest.

key_themes: Iron ore demand weakness — China uncertainty weighing on major miners
NAB job cuts — banking sector under structural cost pressure
Oil price surge — energy sector outperforming
Junior explorer activity — rare earths, gold, and manganese discoveries attracting capital
AI volatility on Wall Street creating mixed ASX spillover
Australian residential property slowdown — Perth bust, falling new home sales
China export surplus as systemic risk to global trade and Australian commodity demand
Fiscal pressure — calls for GST increase and Victorian budget cuts signal government austerity risk

risk_assessment.risk_factor: NAB mass layoffs — banking sector earnings risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce overweight positions in NAB.AX; monitor CBA.AX and WBC.AX for contagion. Favour defensive financials or exit sector temporarily.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price weakness — China demand uncertainty
risk_assessment.mitigation: Trim exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX. Diversify materials exposure toward gold and energy. Monitor Chinese stimulus announcements as potential reversal catalyst.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: AI sector volatility spillover from Wall Street
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid concentrated ASX tech/AI positions. Use options for downside protection on growth names. Prefer quality over speculative AI plays.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Australian residential property bust — Perth leading decline
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to residential developers and property-linked consumer names. Favour commercial or industrial REIT sub-sectors.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: China export surge disrupting Australian trade partners
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor AUD/USD for depreciation pressure. Avoid Australian exporters with direct China price competition exposure (e.g., steel, manufacturing).

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fiscal austerity risk — GST reform and state budget cuts
risk_assessment.mitigation: Watch for consumer spending headwinds. Defensive positioning in consumer staples and healthcare preferred over discretionary.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Oil price surge — input cost inflation for non-energy sectors
risk_assessment.mitigation: Energy sector long positions as hedge. Monitor transport, logistics, and airline cost structures for margin compression.

opportunities.recommendation: Accumulate ASX energy producers on oil price strength
opportunities.rationale: Oil surging with momentum; ASX energy shares already jumping. WDS.AX and STO.AX offer direct leverage to elevated Brent crude prices.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to junior rare earths and gold explorers
opportunities.rationale: Multiple high-grade discoveries in WA and NT (rare earths extending 8km, high-grade gold hits, manganese jackpot) signal active exploration cycle. Small-cap upside for risk-tolerant investors.

opportunities.recommendation: Gold exposure via producers exiting hedging constraints
opportunities.rationale: Kaiser gold loan exit freeing $600K/month for mine growth is a catalyst for re-rating. Broader gold sector benefits from macro uncertainty.

opportunities.recommendation: Maintain defensive healthcare weighting via CSL
opportunities.rationale: CSL.AX offers earnings resilience amid ASX weakness. GLP-1/obesity drug narrative provides additional sector interest.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce NAB exposure; review broad bank sector weighting
defensive_moves.rationale: Mass job cuts at NAB signal structural cost pressure and potential revenue deterioration. Financials sector sentiment soured on the day.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim large-cap iron ore miner positions
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore spooking Vale implies global demand concern. China growth appetite uncertain. BHP and RIO vulnerable to further downside.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid residential property developers; shift to defensive REITs
defensive_moves.rationale: Perth house price bust accelerating, new home sales falling fast. Residential developer earnings at risk.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge ASX broad market exposure via index puts or cash increase
defensive_moves.rationale: ASX slumping despite global AI rebound, iron ore weak, banks cutting jobs, property declining — multiple headwinds converging.

market_outlook.short_term: Cautious to bearish over 1–3 months. ASX faces multiple convergent headwinds: NAB job cuts dampening financial sector sentiment, iron ore weakness pressuring materials, and residential property declining. Energy is the key bright spot. AI volatility from Wall Street adds uncertainty. Expect ASX 200 (^AXJO) to remain under pressure with limited upside catalysts unless China stimulus surprises or commodity prices stabilise.
market_outlook.long_term: Selectively constructive over 6–12 months. Junior explorer cycle in rare earths, gold, and manganese offers upside for risk-tolerant investors. Energy transition materials (rare earths, manganese) align with long-term structural demand. Banking sector may stabilise post-restructuring. Key risk is prolonged China demand weakness or global AI capex disappointment triggering a broader risk-off move.
key_catalysts: RBA rate decision and forward guidance — watch for any pivot signalling
China economic data and stimulus announcements — critical for iron ore and materials
NAB earnings and job cut execution timeline — sector sentiment barometer
Oil price trajectory — sustained rally would amplify energy sector outperformance
AI earnings season results from US majors — Wall Street spillover to ASX tech
Australian CPI and employment data — RBA policy path implications
Rare earths and critical minerals policy announcements — potential re-rating catalyst for junior explorers
watch_list: Iron ore spot price (SGX futures) — key BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX driver
AUD/USD — China demand proxy; watch 0.6200 support level
Brent crude oil price — energy sector tailwind confirmation
NAB.AX share price and sector contagion to CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX
CoreLogic dwelling price indices — Perth and national trend
New home sales monthly data — construction and consumer health indicator
Chinese PMI and trade data — commodity demand leading indicator
RBA meeting minutes and governor commentary
US Federal Reserve commentary — AUD and global risk sentiment driver
